previousEvidence.meaning: Historical evidence remains attributed to its own frozen bytes, not the current canUndo implementation.

api.implementation: Copy self, run existing copy.undo(token:), return true only on success; no duplicated stale/capacity/duplicate rules. False for missing, consumed, expired or otherwise invalid tokens and thrown restore errors.
api.mutationBoundary: Nonmutating read; visible state, revision and live RAM token remain unchanged. Actual undo remains a separate host operation requiring persistence before publication.
api.integrationPurpose: Parent can preserve .forgot notes while their token remains undoable even though their deleted memory ID is absent. This evidence does not claim the parent filter or actual encrypted-store regression is tested by this agent.

addedCoverage: Repeated eligible reads leave memory values/revision unchanged and do not consume the live deletion token; a real undo still succeeds afterward.
Deleted memory remains undoable after useMemory/autoRemember preference changes; actual restoration preserves the new preferences.
Consumed and unknown tokens are false without mutations; later content edits make older tokens stale, and undoing the newer edit restores the older token eligibility.
Procedure approval makes the original pending-add undo ineligible without removing the approved procedure.
Duplicate-content and capacity restore failures return false without state changes; actual undo throws the original category, and resolving the blocker makes that same token valid again.
Eligibility respects exactly fifty retained tokens and the RAM-only relaunch boundary; clear invalidates tokens.
